The Reserve Bank of India issued the RBI Grade B 2026 recruitment notification for 60 Officer posts across three cadres General, DEPR (Department of Economic and Policy Research), and DSIM (Department of Statistics and Information Management). The written exam result is not the final step in UP Home Guard recruitment. The final merit list will be prepared only after combining performance across the written exam, PET/PST, and document verification stages.

CBI Apprentice Vacancy Details 2026

The Central Bank of India has announced a total of 4,500 Apprentice vacancies for the financial year 2026-27, distributed across various states and union territories. Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh reportedly have the largest state-wise allocations. Candidates are advised to refer to the official notification PDF on the bank's recruitment page for the exact state-wise and category-wise vacancy breakup, since detailed figures for every state were not confirmed in the sources reviewed for this article.

Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must meet the educational qualification, age limit, and nationality conditions set by the Central Bank of India to be eligible for the Apprentice post.

Educational Qualification

  • A graduation degree (bachelor's degree) in any discipline from a recognised university or institute.
  • Candidates should have completed graduation on or after 1 January 2022 (some sources indicate the cut-off as 1 January 2021; candidates should verify the exact date on the official notification).
  • Candidates with one year or more of work or training experience after graduation are not eligible, since this scheme is meant for fresh graduates.
  • Candidates who have already completed apprenticeship training, or are currently undergoing apprenticeship training elsewhere, are not eligible.
  • Basic computer knowledge is required.
  • Candidates must be proficient in the local language of the state they are applying for.

Age Limit

Candidates must be between 20 and 28 years of age as on 31 May 2026, meaning they should be born between 31 May 1998 and 31 May 2006 (both dates inclusive).

Category Age Relaxation
OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) 3 years
SC / ST 5 years
PwBD (UR/EWS) 10 years
PwBD (OBC) 13 years
PwBD (SC/ST) 15 years

Candidates should check the official notification for the exact category-wise age relaxation applicable to them.

Salary / Stipend Details

Selected apprentices will receive a fixed monthly stipend of ₹15,000 during the 12-month training period. This is a training stipend rather than a regular salary, and no other allowances or benefits are provided. Completion of the apprenticeship does not guarantee permanent employment with the bank.

Application Fee

The exact application fee amount for the CBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026 was not confirmed in the sources reviewed for this article. Candidates should refer to the official Central Bank of India Apprentice notification PDF on centralbank.bank.in for accurate, category-wise fee details, since this cannot be reliably stated here.

Selection Process

The Central Bank of India Apprentice selection process involves two stages:

  1. Online Written Examination: An objective-type computer-based test with no negative marking for wrong answers.
  2. Local Language Proficiency Test: Candidates who qualify the online exam may need to appear for a test assessing reading, writing, and speaking skills in the local language of the applied state. Candidates who studied the local language at Class 10 or Class 12 level may be exempted from this test, subject to document verification.

Final selection also depends on document verification and meeting the required medical fitness standards set by the bank.

Documents Required at the Exam Centre

  • Printed copy of the CBI Apprentice Admit Card 2026
  • A valid original government-issued photo ID proof, such as Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Passport, Voter ID, or Driving Licence
  • A photocopy of the photo ID for verification
  • Recent passport-size photographs, as specified in the admit card instructions

Candidates should ensure the name on their ID proof matches the name printed on the admit card to avoid denial of entry.

  3. Click on the "CBI Apprentice Admit Card 2026" or "Download Call Letter" link.
  4. Enter your Registration Number/Roll Number and Password or Date of Birth.
  5. Fill in the captcha code, if required.

The Himachal Pradesh Public Service Commission has opened 369 Assistant Professor (College Cadre) vacancies across 22 separate subject-wise notifications (Advertisement No. 34/6-2026 to 55/6-2026), released on 17 June 2026. Each subject has its own application on the HPPSC OTR portal, closing on 15 August 2026 (11:59 PM), with selected candidates engaged as Job Trainees at Rs. 35,000/- per month.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source

Apropos this Commission’s advertisement Nos. 33/6-2026 to 55/6-2026 whereby the post(s) of Assistant Professor (College Cadre) in various disciplines in the Department of Higher Education, H.P. were notified. Now keeping in view the large number of representations received from aspiring candidates requesting extension of the last date for submission of ORA, the date for online recruitment application is hereby extended upto 15.08.2026 till 11:59 P.M.

HPPSC Assistant Professor 2026 - Overview

Particulars Details
Recruiting Body Himachal Pradesh Public Service Commission (HPPSC)
Post Assistant Professor (College Cadre), Group-A (Job Trainee)
Department Department of Higher Education, Himachal Pradesh

About the HPPSC Assistant Professor Recruitment 2026

This is a consolidated drive covering 22 individual subject-wise advertisements for teaching posts in Himachal Pradesh's government colleges, ranging from Hindi and Chemistry to Tabla and Public Administration. Each subject runs as a separate Online Recruitment Application (ORA) on the HPPSC OTR portal, since vacancies, reservation breakup, and advertisement numbers differ from subject to subject, even though age, fee, and selection rules remain identical across all 22.

HPPSC Assistant Professor 2026 - Subject-Wise Vacancies (369 Posts)

The 369 posts are spread unevenly across 22 subjects, with English (39 posts) carrying the largest share, followed by Chemistry and Hindi (34 posts each), while Dance and Tabla have only 2 posts each. All posts, regardless of subject, carry the same Rs. 35,000/- monthly pay.

Category-Wise Reservation

For instance, the English post (39 vacancies) is divided as UR=16, SC=05, ST=03, OBC=02, EWS=04, with the rest under sub-categories, while smaller posts like Dance and Tabla are entirely unreserved. Candidates should verify the category matrix in their subject's specific notification PDF, as it directly affects age relaxation and cut-off eligibility.

Eligibility Criteria

HPPSC requires a Master's degree with at least 55% marks (50% for SC/ST/OBC and PwBD) in the relevant subject, a qualifying NET/SLET/SET score, and an age between 18 and 45 years as on 1 January 2026. The subject of the Master's degree must correspond to the post applied for.

  • Master's degree with 55% marks (or equivalent grade) in the relevant subject from a recognized university, or an equivalent recognized foreign degree.
  • 5% relaxation (55% to 50%) for SC/ST/OBC (non-creamy layer) and Physically/Visually Handicapped candidates.
  • 5% relaxation for Ph.D. holders who completed their Master's before September 1991.
  • NET (UGC/CSIR) or equivalent SLET/SET is the minimum eligibility condition for the post.
  • Ph.D. holders are exempt from NET/SLET/SET, provided the Ph.D. was awarded in regular mode, evaluated by at least two external examiners, included an open viva-voce, and is backed by at least two published papers (one refereed) plus two conference presentations.
  • Candidates who qualified SET-2026 are also eligible; the window will reopen for them if the SET-2026 result comes after the regular closing date.

The age is calculated as on 1 January 2026, based on the Matriculation certificate. A 5-year relaxation in upper age applies only to Bonafide SC/ST/OBC, Ward of Freedom Fighters, and Persons with Disabilities of HP, and only if the post is reserved for that category in the subject applied for; HP Government employees and Ex-Servicemen get relaxation per separate government instructions.

Application Fee and How to Apply

The application fee is a flat Rs. 600 for all candidates, paid online via Debit Card, Credit Card, UPI, or other digital modes, and is non-refundable and non-transferable once paid. Since each subject is a separate application, the fee must be paid afresh for every subject applied to.

  1. Visit http://www.hppsc.hp.gov.in/hppsc.
  2. Click "Apply Online" on the homepage.
  3. Select "One Time Registration (OTR) for Examinations" and complete registration if new.
  4. Log in to the OTR account and view live advertisements on the dashboard.
  5. Select the relevant subject advertisement (e.g., Hindi – 47/6-2026, History – 48/6-2026) and fill the form.
  6. Upload scanned Matriculation certificate, degree/marksheets, category certificate, and Bonafide HP certificate.
  7. Pay the Rs. 600 fee online.
  8. Confirm the undertaking on document legibility and submit the final application.
  9. Download the confirmation/printout for records.

Once submitted, no corrections or modifications are allowed, so candidates should verify every field before final submission.

Documents Required for Upload

Applications with missing or poor-quality scans are liable to rejection, so candidates should keep the following ready: Matriculation certificate for age proof, degree certificates with all years' marksheets, experience certificate (wherever required), and valid category certificates (SC/ST/OBC/EWS/Ex-Servicemen/WFF/PwBD) in the HP Government's prescribed format. Reserved category candidates additionally need a Bonafide Himachali certificate, and EWS applicants need an Income & Asset Certificate or a BDO-countersigned BPL Certificate along with a non-SC/ST/OBC certificate.

Selection Process

Selection runs through a two-paper written test on the same day, followed by a Personality Test, with final merit based on Paper-II plus interview marks. The process starts with document scrutiny and ends with a 30-mark interview at HPPSC's Shimla office.

Stage Component Details
1 Application Scrutiny Eligible candidates provisionally admitted; rejected candidates get 10 days to represent
2 Paper-I: Screening Test 1-hour MCQ, 100 marks (HP GK-30, National/International Affairs-30, Hindi-20, English-20); qualifying only
3 Paper-II: Subject Aptitude Test (SAT) 3-hour descriptive test, 120 marks, subject-specific syllabus; held same day as Paper-I
4 Document Verification Shortlisting per category-wise zone ratio (1:5 for 11+ posts; 1:5+3 for up to 10 posts)
5 Personality Test 30 marks, at HPPSC office Shimla only; minimum pass 40% General / 30% Reserved
6 Final Merit SAT (120) + Personality Test (30) = 150 marks total

Paper-I is qualifying only and does not count toward merit; candidates scoring zero or negative marks are excluded outright. There is 0.25 mark negative marking per wrong, multiple, or blank answer in objective tests, and the SAT qualifying mark is 45% General / 40% Reserved.

Salary

Selected candidates are engaged as Job Trainees at a fixed Rs. 35,000/- per month, uniform across all 22 subjects, under the Department of Personnel's notification No. Per(AP)-C-B(15)-3/2024 dated 19 July 2025, which governs the job-trainee engagement scheme across HP Government departments.

Important Dates

Last Date to Apply Online 15 August 2026, 11:59 PM
Last Date for Fee Payment 15 August 2026, 11:59 PM
Screening Test / SAT Exam To be announced

Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Applying under the wrong subject advertisement number: With 22 separate codes (34/6-2026 to 55/6-2026), an incorrect subject selection cannot be corrected after submission.
  • Uploading unclear documents: Illegible scanned certificates lead to rejection, so scan at adequate resolution.
  • Submitting without a final review: No corrections are allowed post-submission, so date of birth and category should be double-checked beforehand.
  • Skipping NET/SLET/SET proof upload: Missing this can cause provisional rejection even for otherwise eligible candidates.
  • Missing the answer key objection window: Objections to the Paper-I key must be raised within 5 days of publication with Rs. 100 per question; this window cannot be reopened.
  • Assuming blanket relaxation: Age and qualification relaxations apply only if the post is reserved for that category in the specific subject.

RRB Technician Eligibility Criteria 2026

Anyone wondering who can apply for RRB Technician 2026 should know that eligibility depends on educational qualification, age limit, and medical standards specific to each post. The qualification requirements vary by department, and candidates must satisfy these conditions on or before the closing date, 29 July 2026, since those awaiting final results are not eligible to apply.

Educational Qualification

For Technician Grade-I Signal, candidates need a Bachelor of Science in Physics/Electronics/Computer Science/Information Technology/Instrumentation, a three-year diploma in Engineering, or a Degree in Engineering in these streams. For most Technician Grade-III posts, candidates need Matriculation/SSLC plus ITI from NCVT/SCVT or Matriculation/SSLC plus Course Completed Act Apprenticeship in the relevant trade (such as Fitter, Welder, Electrician, Machinist, Carpenter, or Blacksmith, depending on the post applied for).

Age Relaxation

Candidates from reserved categories get standard relaxation in the upper age limit: 5 years for SC/ST, 3 years for OBC-NCL, and additional relaxation for PwBD candidates (10 years for UR/EWS, 13 years for OBC-NCL, 15 years for SC/ST). Ex-servicemen get age relaxation equal to their length of service plus 3 years (UR/EWS), 6 years (OBC-NCL), or 8 years (SC/ST) after deducting service length from their actual age.

RRB Technician Application Fee 2026

The application fee for RRB Technician CEN 02/2026 differs by candidate category and is partially refundable for those who appear in the CBT. General category candidates pay more than reserved categories, with both fee structures eligible for partial refund upon attending the exam.

RRB Technician Selection Process 2026

Candidates often ask how RRB selects Technicians, and the answer is a three-stage process based purely on merit. The recruitment involves a Computer Based Test (CBT), Document Verification (DV), and a Medical Examination, with shortlisting at each stage determined by performance in the previous one.

  1. Computer Based Test (CBT): A single CBT of 90 minutes with 100 questions and negative marking of 1/3rd mark per wrong answer. Minimum qualifying marks are 40% (UR/EWS), 30% (OBC-NCL/SC), and 25% (ST).
  2. Document Verification (DV): Candidates are shortlisted at a 1:1 ratio against vacancies based on CBT merit, RRB-wise. Original documents must be produced; no extra time is given for missing certificates.
  3. Medical Examination (ME): Conducted by Railway Medical Authorities as per the medical standard (A3, B1, B2, or C1) prescribed for the specific post.

Based on typical RRB recruitment cycles, CBT is expected a few months after the application closes, followed by DV and medical examination in subsequent phases - though exact dates will be announced on official RRB websites.

RRB Technician CEN 02/2026 Apply Online

The RRB Technician Apply Online link will be active from 30 June 2026 on all official RRB portals. Candidates must select their nearest or preferred RRB zone from the list below and complete the "Create an Account" step before proceeding to the actual application form.

How to Apply for RRB Technician CEN 02/2026

Candidates wanting to apply online for RRB Technician 2026 need to first create an account before filling the application form. The process is entirely online, and applicants must choose only one RRB per pay level since selecting more than one RRB for the same pay level leads to rejection of all applications.

  1. Visit the official RRB website relevant to your region or the centralised portal at rrb.indianrailways.gov.in.
  2. Click on "Create an Account" and enter your name, father's name, mother's name, and date of birth exactly as per your Matriculation certificate.
  3. Use DigiLocker or Aadhaar for identity authentication to ensure smoother verification later.
  4. Log in and fill the online application form, selecting your preferred RRB and Pay Level (5 or 2).
  5. Provide order of preference for posts under the chosen RRB and Pay Level.
  6. Capture your live photograph through webcam or mobile camera as instructed (pre-existing photos are not accepted).
  7. Upload your signature in JPG/JPEG format (30–49 KB, black ink on white paper, running handwriting).
  8. Pay the examination fee online through net banking, debit/credit card, or UPI.
  9. Submit the application and save the registration number for future reference.

RRB Technician Salary and Pay Scale 2026

Candidates curious about RRB Technician in-hand salary should note that pay depends on the post and pay level assigned. Technician Grade-I Signal carries a higher starting pay than Technician Grade-III posts, as shown below.

Post 7th CPC Pay Level Initial Pay
Technician Grade-I Signal Level-5 ₹29,200
Technician Grade-III (all categories) Level-2 ₹19,900

Selected candidates will undergo training wherever prescribed, during which only a stipend is paid rather than full pay.

RRB Technician Document Requirements

Candidates shortlisted for Document Verification must carry all original certificates along with two sets of self-attested photocopies. Required documents include Matriculation/educational qualification certificates, ITI/Apprenticeship certificates, caste/category certificates (SC/ST/OBC-NCL/EWS as applicable in the prescribed Annexure format), a valid original photo ID, and an NOC from the current employer if already employed in government service.

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying for RRB Technician 2026

Many candidates lose their candidature due to avoidable errors rather than ineligibility. Being aware of these common pitfalls can help applicants submit a clean, error-free application the first time.

  • Entering wrong name/DOB: Details in "Create an Account" cannot be changed later - always match them exactly with your Matriculation certificate.
  • Applying to multiple RRBs for the same Pay Level: This leads to rejection of all applications and debarment from future RRB/RRC exams.
  • Uploading a pre-existing or printed photo: Only live-captured photographs are accepted; printed photo uploads cause summary rejection.
  • Signature in capital/block letters: Signatures must be in cursive running handwriting with black ink - block letters are grounds for rejection.
  • Missing the fee payment deadline: Fee must be paid by 31 July 2026, two days after the application deadline - don't assume submission alone is enough.
  • Ignoring the modification window: Errors (other than account details and chosen RRB) can be corrected only between 1–10 August 2026 by paying ₹250 per modification.

Educational Qualification

Candidates who are in the final year of their Engineering Degree programme and are yet to receive their final results may also apply, provided they fulfil all other eligibility criteria. Recruitment Criteria

IHMCL Recruitment 2026: Selection Process

Selection for the post of Systems Engineer (ITS) is based on the following criteria:

  • Merit is determined on the basis of the valid GATE Score of the year 2025.
  • IHMCL reserves the right to invite candidates for interview as per a cut-off for the respective category, to be decided subsequently by IHMCL.
  • If the number of applications received is large, IHMCL will adopt a shortlisting criterion to restrict the number of candidates called for interaction/interview to a reasonable number, by a method decided by the Selection Committee.
  • For the final merit list, if two or more candidates in the same category have equal scores/marks, the candidate older in age will be placed higher in the merit list.

Note: Candidates must enter their GATE Score as mentioned in the official GATE 2025 Scorecard (range: 0 to 1000) while applying.

IHMCL Recruitment 2026: Reservation Guidelines

  • Reservation benefit under community categories is available only if the candidate's caste is included in the list of reserved communities issued by the Central Government.
  • OBC candidates must submit an OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) certificate issued during the year 2026-2027, clearly indicating that the candidate does not belong to the creamy layer.
  • EWS candidates must meet the criteria issued by the Central Government and possess an Income & Asset Certificate based on income for Financial Year 2025-2026, issued after 1 April 2026.
  • Candidates seeking reservation as SC/ST/OBC-NCL/EWS must submit a certificate in the prescribed proforma only, from the designated authority, with the caste/community name and spelling exactly matching the central government's notified lists.
  • No change in the community status already indicated in the online application will be allowed.
  • Candidates who fail to submit valid Caste/Category certificates will not be considered for reservation; if otherwise eligible under Unreserved (UR) criteria, their candidature will be considered against the UR vacancy only.

  4. Follow the on-screen instructions and fill up the application form with the requisite information.
  5. Upload all required documents: photograph, signature, Class X certificate, caste/category certificate (if applicable), Engineering degree passing certificate, and GATE Score Card 2025.
  6. Click "Next" to preview the application.
  7. Use the "Edit" option if any correction is needed, or click the final "Submit" button once satisfied.
  8. Upon submission, a Unique Reference Number along with an "Application Acknowledgement" will be generated automatically and sent to the registered email address.
  9. Keep a copy of the Application Acknowledgement safely for future submission to IHMCL along with supporting documents.

Applications must be submitted online by 2 August 2026 (6:00 PM). Applications received through any mode other than online will not be accepted and will be summarily rejected.

IHMCL Recruitment 2026: Important Instructions

  • The posts carry all-India service liability; only candidates willing to serve anywhere in India should apply.
  • Candidates are advised to fill the online application carefully, as no request for alteration/modification of entries will be entertained after submission.
  • In case of multiple applications by the same candidate, only the last submitted application will be considered; earlier applications will be rejected.

  • Candidates must not furnish false, tampered, or fabricated particulars, or suppress material information.
  • All selected candidates must execute a Service Bond of Rs. 3.00 lakh at the time of joining, for serving IHMCL for a minimum period of 3 years. If a candidate resigns before the bond period expires, or their service is terminated due to misconduct within three years, they must deposit Rs. 3.0 lakh to IHMCL. IHMCL does not entertain transfer of service bonds for selected candidates working in other organizations.
  • Canvassing or bringing influence in any form will disqualify the candidature.
  • Any Corrigendum, Addendum, or Cancellation to the advertisement will be published only on the IHMCL website, not in newspapers.
  • The advertisement can be withdrawn at any time at the discretion of the Competent Authority, without assigning any reason.

ICSIL Recruitment 2026 Vacancy Details

This notification is issued solely to create a panel of eligible candidates for present and future manpower requirements of various client departments. Application Fee

Selection Process

Empanelment under this notification is based on the application ID sequence, followed by document verification and, where required, an interview or interaction conducted by the client department.

  • Candidates found eligible after scrutiny of age, educational qualification, experience and other prescribed conditions will be empanelled.
  • Where the client department makes the final selection, empanelled candidates are sent for consideration in a ratio of 1:3, in increasing order of Application ID. Candidates not selected are placed back in the panel at the end.
  • Where ICSIL itself deploys manpower, empanelled candidates are sent as per increasing Application ID for the number required by the department.
  • Candidates may be called for interview, interaction, or any other selection process prescribed by the client department. Absence at this stage will lead to cancellation of selection.
  • Empanelment, a lower Application ID, or participation in the process does not confer any right to interview, selection, deployment or engagement.

Required Documents

Candidates must carry original documents along with self-attested photocopies for verification.

  • Original documents relating to age, educational qualification, experience and identity proof

  4. Ensure the profile matches the eligibility criteria mentioned in the notification for the post applied for.
  5. Candidates can update their profile as needed.
  6. Submit the application within the window: 06:00 PM on 04/07/2026 to 06:00 PM on 11/07/2026.

  • Selected candidates may be deployed anywhere in Delhi/NCR and may be required to work in shifts or rotational duties. No additional conveyance allowance will be paid.
  • No TA/DA is admissible for attending document verification, interview, interaction or any stage of the selection process.
  • Fifteen days' salary will be retained as a refundable security deposit, in two equal instalments from the first two months' salary. It will be refunded with applicable savings bank interest on completion of the contractual period and submission of a No Dues Certificate.
  • The engagement remains valid for the prescribed contractual period or until a regular incumbent joins the post, whichever is earlier.
  • Canvassing in any form, including seeking recommendations or lobbying, will lead to immediate disqualification and may affect eligibility for future opportunities with ICSIL.
  • If any information or document submitted is found false, fabricated, misleading or incorrect, the candidature or engagement will be cancelled without notice.

Eligibility Criteria

Educational Qualification

Candidates applying for ICAI Branch In-Charge Recruitment 2026 must be a Graduate from a recognized University. Educational qualifications must be from a University, Deemed University, or Institution recognized by AICTE, UGC, or the appropriate statutory authority.

Skill Sets Required

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills with proficiency in spoken and written English.
  • Proficiency in MS Office and other relevant computer applications.
  • Effective managerial, administrative, and organizational abilities.
  • Strong relationship management and conflict resolution skills.

Work Experience Requirement

Only post-qualification, full-time work experience is counted. Part-time or freelancing work is not considered. Articleship, internship, or training experience that forms part of a qualification requirement is not counted towards years of work experience. Category-wise experience requirements are listed in the salary table below.

Age Limit

Candidates must be between 27 and 40 years of age as on 30th June 2026 to be eligible for ICAI Branch In-Charge Recruitment 2026.

Salary / Pay Scale

The compensation offered for the Branch In-Charge post varies by Branch Category, based on the minimum post-qualification experience required. Compensation includes Basic Pay, Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance, and National Pension System (NPS), along with Leave Travel Concession, Gratuity, and other benefits as per service conditions.

  • Category-I Branches: Minimum 5 years of experience - Compensation of approximately ₹7.45 lakhs per annum.
  • Category-II Branches: Minimum 5 years of experience - Compensation of approximately ₹6.33 lakhs per annum.
  • Category-III Branches: Minimum 5 years of experience - Compensation of approximately ₹5.59 lakhs per annum.
  • Category-IV Branches: Minimum 3 years of experience - Compensation of approximately ₹4.84 lakhs per annum.
  • Category-V & VI Branches: Minimum 3 years of experience - Compensation of approximately ₹4.10 lakhs per annum.
Branch Category Minimum Post-Qualification Experience Compensation Offered (Approx.)
Category-I 5 years ₹7.45 lakhs per annum
Category-II 5 years ₹6.33 lakhs per annum
Category-III 5 years ₹5.59 lakhs per annum
Category-IV 3 years ₹4.84 lakhs per annum
Category-V & VI 3 years ₹4.10 lakhs per annum

Application Fee

Candidates are required to pay an application fee of ₹250 (Rupees Two Hundred and Fifty only), non-refundable and inclusive of all applicable taxes, through the online portal. An application will be treated as complete only after successful payment of the fee; incomplete applications are liable to be rejected.

Selection Process

The selection process for ICAI Branch In-Charge Recruitment 2026 consists of a Computer Based Test (CBT) followed by an Interview.

Computer Based Test (CBT)

Parameter Details
Mode of Examination Computer Based Test (CBT)
Medium / Language English
Question Paper Type Multiple Choice Questions (MCQ) + Descriptive
Total Marks 425
Exam Duration 180 minutes
Minimum Qualifying Marks 170

CBT Syllabus and Marks Distribution

Module Name Number of Questions Total Marks
English Comprehension 25 100
E-Mail Writing 2 50
Intermediate Level MS Excel 20 80
Intermediate Level MS Word 18 72
General Awareness 12 48
Basic Accounting 30 75
Total 107 425

Candidates can select their preferred test centre through the online portal. Centre allotment is made solely based on availability of seats and candidate preference, and no request for change of centre is entertained. ICAI reserves the right to cancel or add test cities depending on administrative feasibility.

Interview

Candidates who qualify the CBT will be called for an Interview. The minimum qualifying marks for the Interview are 30. Marks obtained in the Interview are added to the CBT marks to prepare the final merit list. Before the interview, ICAI will verify submitted document copies against originals; candidates with discrepancies will not be permitted to appear. No TA/DA is paid for attending the interview.

Also read: SSC SSA Recruitment 2026 Notification Out

Required Documents

Candidates must upload all required documents in the prescribed format at the time of submitting the online application. Incomplete forms or illegible documents can lead to rejection of candidature at any stage of the recruitment process. Original educational certificates and other documents will be required for verification at the time of the Interview.

How to Apply

  1. Visit the official ICAI website and locate the Branch In-Charge Recruitment 2026 notification (Advertisement No. 01/2026/HRD/BHRS/07).
  2. Click on the online application / "Apply Here" link provided in the notification.
  3. Register with a valid, active email ID and mobile number.
  4. Fill in the online application form with personal, educational, and experience details.
  5. Select your preferred region and give up to three branch location preferences.
  6. Upload all required documents in the prescribed format.
  7. Pay the application fee of ₹250 online.
  8. Submit the form and save a printout for future reference.

Only online applications are accepted. Applications received by post, hand, email, or any other mode will not be considered. The last date to apply online is 19th July 2026.

Important Instructions

  • ICAI reserves the right to increase, decrease, or cancel vacancies, or the entire recruitment process, without assigning any reason.
  • Candidates must fulfil the minimum eligibility criteria of age and post-qualification experience as on 30th June 2026.
  • Applications with false information, suppressed facts, or misrepresentation are liable to be rejected, and candidates may be debarred from future recruitment.
  • Candidates should not send hard copies of their application, CV, or certificates to ICAI.
  • Candidates may apply for branches of one region only, giving up to three preferred branch locations, irrespective of Branch Category. Multiple or duplicate applications may lead to disqualification.
  • Selected candidates may be posted at any branch at ICAI's discretion, irrespective of preferences given.
  • Candidates employed in Central/State Government, Public Sector Enterprises, or Autonomous Bodies must produce a No Objection Certificate at the time of Interview.
  • Educational qualifications of shortlisted candidates will be verified from the respective University, Board, Institute, or Organisation.
  • Selected candidates will be on probation for one year, which may be extended for non-satisfactory performance.
  • Canvassing in any form will lead to disqualification.
  • Any notification or corrigendum will be published only on the official ICAI website; it is the applicant's responsibility to keep checking for updates.

Selection Process

The selection process for Indian Army Sports Quota Recruitment 2026 involves shortlisting based on sports achievements, followed by trials and medical examination.

MPESB Krishi Vistar Adhikari Selection Process 2026

The selection for the Agriculture Extension Officer post will be made through a single online written exam followed by document verification. There is no interview.

  1. Online Written Exam (CBT): Objective-type paper of 200 marks conducted by MPESB.
  2. Normalization: If the exam is held in multiple shifts, results are prepared using the Normalised Equi-Percentile (NEP) scaling technique.
  3. Merit List and Waiting List: MPESB prepares a post-wise merit list; a waiting list of 15% of the total posts remains valid for one year or until the next exam result, whichever is earlier.
  4. Document Verification: Certificates are verified by the Farmer Welfare and Agriculture Development Department, not by MPESB.
  5. Appointment: Appointment orders are to be issued within a maximum of three months from the date of the selection list.

Minimum Qualifying Marks

  • Unreserved (UR): 50% marks
  • SC / ST / OBC / EWS / Divyangjan: 40% marks (after 10% relaxation)

EWS candidates get the 10% relaxation in qualifying marks, but their selection is made on merit from the EWS list.

MPESB Krishi Vistar Adhikari Exam Pattern 2026

The exam consists of a single question paper of 200 marks with two parts, to be solved in 3 hours.

Part A General Knowledge, General Hindi, General English, General Maths, General Reasoning Ability, General Science, General Computer Knowledge 100
Part B Subject-based questions (Agriculture / Horticulture) 100

  • Questions are objective (MCQ) type with four options each, in Hindi and English medium.
  • Each correct answer carries 1 mark.
  • Negative marking applies: 0.25 marks are deducted for every wrong answer, as per clause 3.8 of the official rulebook.
  • After the exam, candidates must confirm their RAW score (number of correct answers) displayed on the computer screen before submitting.
  • Objections against questions can be filed online within three days of the objection link going live, with a fee of Rs. 150 per question.
  • There is no provision for re-evaluation or re-totalling after the result is declared.

MPESB Krishi Vistar Adhikari Syllabus 2026

Part A: General Subjects (100 Marks)

  • General Knowledge
  • General Hindi
  • General English
  • General Maths
  • General Reasoning Ability
  • General Science
  • General Computer Knowledge

Part B: Agriculture Subject Syllabus (100 Marks)

  1. General Agriculture: Agriculture and its importance in the national economy.
  2. Agronomy: Major crops of MP, agro-techniques of major field crops of MP, farming systems and sustainable agriculture, introductory agro-meteorology, agro-climatic and agro-ecological zones.
  3. Soil Science: Soil composition and its role in crop production; physical, chemical and biological properties of soil; essential plant nutrients, their functions and dynamics; integrated nutrient management; problem soils and their management.
  4. Soil and Water Conservation: Watershed management.
  5. Plant Physiology: Absorption, translocation and metabolism of nutrients; photosynthesis and respiration; growth and development; growth regulators.
  6. Crop Improvement: Elements of genetics and plant breeding as applied to crop improvement.
  7. Horticulture: Package of practices for important fruits, vegetables, spices and flowering plants; nursery management and propagation methods; physiological disorders and their management; post-harvest management and value addition.
  8. Plant Protection: Important insect pests and diseases and their management; integrated pest and disease management; spray equipment selection and maintenance; rodent management; pesticide safety precautions.
  9. Agricultural Economics: Principles of economics applied to agriculture; farm planning and resource management; farming systems; marketing of agricultural produce and regulated markets in MP (including e-Chaupal); pricing of agricultural produce.
  10. Agricultural Extension Education: Philosophy, objectives and principles of extension; extension organisations at state, district and block levels; communication methods; role of farmers' organisations; role and importance of training; important rural development programmes in India.

Eligibility for IBPS Specialist Officer Recruitment 2026 depends on the specific post applied for, since each role has a distinct educational qualification requirement. Age limits, however, remain uniform across all six posts, with relaxations available for reserved categories.

Agricultural Field Officer 4-year degree in Agriculture/Horticulture/Animal Husbandry/Veterinary Science/Dairy Science/Fishery Science or allied subjects

IBPS Specialist Officer Selection Process 2026

Selection under IBPS CRP SPL-XVI 2026 follows a three-stage process: Online Preliminary Examination, Online Main Examination, and a Common Interview. Only candidates who clear each stage progress to the next, and the final merit list is based on Main Examination and Interview scores combined.

  1. Online Preliminary Examination – Tentatively in August 2026; candidates must clear individual cut-offs in each of four tests.
  2. Preliminary Result – Declared in September/October 2026.
  3. Online Main Examination – Tentatively in November 2026; scores from this stage alone are used for interview shortlisting and final merit.
  4. Main Exam Result – Declared in November 2026.
  5. Common Interview – Conducted by Participating Banks and coordinated by Nodal Banks in November/December 2026; total 100 marks with minimum qualifying marks of 40% (35% for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD).
  6. Provisional Allotment – Expected in January 2027, based on merit-cum-preference with an 80:20 weightage between Main Exam and Interview.

Exam Pattern Overview

The Preliminary Exam for IT Officer, Agricultural Field Officer, HR/Personnel Officer, and Marketing Officer consists of 100 questions for 125 marks across English Language, Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, and Professional Knowledge, to be completed in 80 minutes. The Main Exam for the same posts carries 150 objective questions for 200 marks plus a Descriptive Paper of 25 marks, totaling 225 marks in 155 minutes. Law Officer and Rajbhasha Adhikari have a similar structure but include General Awareness with Special Reference to Banking Industry in place of Quantitative Aptitude.

There is a penalty of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer in objective tests; no penalty applies for unattempted questions.

IBPS CRP SPL-XVI Apply Online 2026

Candidates can apply for IBPS Specialist Officer Recruitment 2026 only through the online mode on the official IBPS website; no other application method is accepted. The steps below outline the complete registration and payment process.

  1. Visit the official website www.ibps.in and click on the "CRP SPL" link on the homepage.
  2. Select "Click Here to Apply Online for CRP-Specialist Officers (CRP SPL-XVI)" to open the application form.
  3. Click "Click Here for New Registration" and enter basic details to generate a Provisional Registration Number and Password.
  4. Log in again using the provisional credentials to complete the application form.
  5. Upload photograph, signature, left thumb impression, handwritten declaration, and SSC/SSLC/10th standard certificate as per specifications.
  6. Capture and upload a live photograph via webcam or mobile phone.
  7. Verify all details carefully, since no changes are allowed after clicking "Complete Registration" (except during the 2-day Edit Window).
  8. Pay the applicable application fee online via Debit Card, Credit Card, Net Banking, or UPI.
  9. Download and print the system-generated application form and e-receipt for future reference.

IBPS CRP SPL-XVI Document Requirements

Shortlisted candidates must produce original documents along with self-attested photocopies at the time of interview, failing which their candidature can be cancelled. Required documents include the interview call letter, system-generated application printout, proof of date of birth, photo identity proof, educational mark sheets/certificates, and category certificates (SC/ST/OBC-NCL/EWS/PwBD) as applicable, all in prescribed Government of India formats.

OBC candidates must submit a Non-Creamy Layer certificate issued on or after 01.04.2026, while EWS candidates need an Income & Asset Certificate valid for the year 2026-27 for financial year 2025-26.

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying for IBPS CRP SPL-XVI

Many candidates lose their chance at IBPS Specialist Officer Recruitment 2026 due to avoidable errors during the application process. Being aware of these common mistakes in advance can help ensure a smooth, error-free submission.

  • Applying for multiple posts: A candidate can apply for only one post; multiple applications are summarily rejected.
  • Uploading incorrect photo/signature size: Photos must be 4.5cm × 3.5cm (20-50 KB), and signatures 10-20 KB; oversized or blurred files cause application rejection.
  • Writing the declaration in capital letters: The handwritten declaration must be in the candidate's own handwriting, in English, and NOT in capital letters.
  • Ignoring the Edit Window: Since most fields like Name, Email ID, Mobile Number, and Nationality cannot be edited after submission, double-check all entries before final submission.
  • Missing the fee payment deadline: Applying without completing fee payment within 01.07.2026 to 21.07.2026 renders the form incomplete and invalid.
  • Not retaining photograph copies: Candidates should keep at least 8 copies of the uploaded photograph, as these are required at multiple stages including exam day.

How to Apply for Sarkari Job Online 2026

  2. Read the official notification: Click on the job listing to open the official notification PDF. Read all eligibility conditions — age limit, educational qualification, experience, category relaxations.

  3. Visit the official recruitment website: Never apply through third-party sites. Use the direct official link provided on OnlyJobs. Look for "Apply Online" or "Register" on the official portal.

  4. Register / Create account: Sign up using your valid email ID and active mobile number. Keep your Aadhaar, bank account details, and email accessible.

  5. Fill the application form: Enter personal details, educational qualifications, category (General/OBC/SC/ST/EWS), address, and other required information accurately.

  6. Upload documents: Scan and upload recent passport-size photograph, signature, 10th certificate (for DOB proof), educational certificates, caste certificate (if applicable). Check file size and format (JPG/PDF as specified).

  7. Pay application fee: Pay via Net Banking, UPI, Debit/Credit Card as applicable. Some categories (SC/ST/PwD/Women) may be exempted from fee. Keep the payment receipt.

  8. Submit and save confirmation: Review all details before final submission. After submitting, download the application printout / PDF confirmation with your registration number. Store it safely for admit card, exam, and future reference.

Age limit is 18 to 35 years as of 1st January 2026 in most states. SC/ST candidates get 5 years relaxation (maximum age 40). OBC candidates get 3 years relaxation (maximum age 38). PwD candidates get additional relaxation as per state rules.

What documents are required for Anganwadi job application?

Required documents: Aadhaar card, 10th/12th marksheet and certificate, domicile/residence certificate, caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), passport-size photograph, scanned signature, and EWS/PwD certificate if applicable. Graduation certificate is needed for Supervisor post applications.

What is ICDS recruitment 2026?

ICDS stands for Integrated Child Development Services - the government programme under which Anganwadi centres operate nationwide. ICDS recruitment 2026 refers to hiring of Anganwadi Workers, Helpers, Supervisors, and CDPOs by state WCD departments under the Ministry of Women & Child Development (wcd.nic.in).

Is Anganwadi Worker a permanent government job?

Anganwadi Workers and Helpers are honorary workers, not regular government employees. They receive a fixed monthly honorarium (not salary) and are entitled to benefits like ESI, health insurance, and maternity benefits. Supervisors and CDPOs are regular government employees in most states and receive full pay & grade pay.

Can I apply for Anganwadi job from a different district?

No. Anganwadi Workers and Helpers must be permanent residents of the same ward/village/district where the vacancy exists. A domicile or residence certificate is mandatory. Applications from outside the specified locality are rejected. For Supervisor/CDPO posts, the same district residency rule generally applies.

Education Qualification for Forest Guard, Forester, Ranger

  • Document Verification: Shortlisted candidates must produce original certificates of age, qualification, caste, residence, sports/NCC and other documents mentioned in the notification.
  • Medical Examination: Many forest posts require medical fitness to ensure candidates can perform field duties in forests, wildlife areas and difficult terrain.

Two Types of No Exam Govt Jobs

No-exam recruitment in India falls into two patterns, and knowing which one a notification belongs to tells you exactly what to prepare for:

Type Typical Posts Who it's for How Selection Works
Fresher - no exam, usually no interview Apprentice, GDS, trainee 10th/12th/ITI/Diploma/Graduate pass Merit list prepared from academic marks
Experienced - no exam, interview-based Officer, manager, specialist, medical Professionals with relevant work experience Shortlisting based on qualification/experience, followed by a personal interview

How Recruitment Without Exam Works in Government Jobs

This section explains the different routes through which government departments fill vacancies without conducting a written competitive exam.

1. Direct Recruitment

Certain senior and specialised posts - such as Chairman, Member, and Secretary in Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (PSCs) - are filled through direct recruitment based on eligibility criteria like qualifications, experience, and domain expertise, rather than a written exam. Similarly, some administrative posts in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) may be filled through direct recruitment.

2. Sports Quota Recruitment

Government organisations such as Indian Railways, the Indian Army, and Public Sector Banks reserve a quota of posts for candidates with outstanding achievements in sports at the state, national, or international level. Eligible candidates can be appointed to posts like Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, and Clerk without going through the regular written exam.

3. Cultural Quota Recruitment

Indian Railways also recruits individuals with exceptional talent in arts, fine arts, music, or literature under the cultural quota for posts such as Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, and Assistant Loco Pilot.

4. Internal Promotions and Deputation

Government departments, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), promote existing employees to higher posts based on performance, seniority, and experience - without requiring them to clear a fresh competitive exam. Ex-servicemen and defence personnel are also often considered for civilian government posts through deputation or reservation quotas, without a written exam.

5. Apprenticeships and Trainee Programmes

Railways, PSUs, and central organisations like DRDO and BEL regularly hire Act Apprentices, Trade Apprentices, and Project Trainees through merit lists based on academic marks - with no written entrance test.

6. Walk-in Interviews

Some government and PSU organisations directly call candidates for walk-in interviews based on their qualifications and experience, especially for technical, medical, and contractual roles.

Government Jobs Without Exam by Sector

This section breaks down no-exam opportunities by sector - banking and railways - which are among the most common areas where such recruitment occurs.

Bank Jobs Without Exam

While most public sector bank recruitment (PO, Clerk, SO) happens through IBPS or bank-specific written exams, some banks fill specific posts - such as Local Bank Officer and certain Specialist Officer roles - through direct recruitment, where the bank shortlists applications based on eligibility criteria and conducts an interview instead of a written test.

Railway Jobs Without Exam

Indian Railways and the various Railway Recruitment Boards/Cells (RRBs/RRCs) offer no-exam entry through:

  • Act Apprentices (selection via academic merit list)
  • Sports Quota posts (Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, Clerk)
  • Cultural Quota posts (Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, Assistant Loco Pilot)
  • Scouts and Guides Quota

Before You Apply: How to Spot Fake "No Exam" Job Offers

No-exam recruitment is the single biggest magnet for job fraud in India, because "direct joining, no exam" is exactly what scammers promise. Four rules protect you:

  1. No genuine government post is ever sold. Nobody - agent, "officer", consultancy - can arrange selection for money. The only payment in real recruitment is the application fee, paid on the official portal, typically a few hundred rupees.
  2. Verify the notification on the official domain. Every real notice lives on a .gov.in, .nic.in or official PSU domain. Every row in our list links to the post page where the official notification PDF and apply link are attached - if an offer you received isn't traceable to an official notice, treat it as fraud.
  3. No recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram DMs. Forwarded "joining letters" and interview calls demanding a deposit are scams, full stop.
  4. Cross-check suspicious notices against PIB Fact Check before sharing or paying anything.

How to Apply for Government Jobs Without Exam

  1. Open the post from the live list and read the official notification PDF - eligibility, age limits and fee are final there, not in any summary.
  2. Confirm you match the qualification and category requirements before paying any fee.
  3. Apply on the official portal linked in the notification; keep the registration number and fee receipt.
  4. For merit-list posts (GDS, apprentice), enter marks exactly as on your certificates - mismatches reject applications at verification.
  5. Track the post page for merit list / shortlist updates, or subscribe to WhatsApp/Telegram alerts so deadlines and results reach you automatically.

Government Jobs Without Exam - FAQs

1. Are there really government jobs without an exam?

Yes. Apprenticeship intakes, India Post GDS, sports and cultural quota posts, walk-in interviews and direct recruitment for experienced candidates are all filled without a written competitive exam. The live list at the top of this page shows every such notification currently open.

2. Which government jobs have no exam and no interview at all?

India Post GDS and Railway/PSU Act Apprentice selections use only a merit list of academic marks - there is no written test and no interview. Everything depends on your Class 10 (and ITI/diploma, where applicable) percentage.

3. What no-exam options exist for freshers after 10th, 12th or ITI?

Apprenticeships, GDS and trainee posts are the main fresher routes. Selection is a merit list prepared from academic marks, which is why these notifications attract very high application volumes despite no exam.

4. Can experienced professionals get a government job without an exam?

Yes. PSUs and autonomous bodies fill officer, manager and specialist posts by shortlisting candidates on qualification and experience, followed by a personal interview - no written test.

5. Are government jobs without exam permanent?

Often not. Apprenticeships are roughly one-year training engagements with a stipend, and many walk-in posts are contractual with fixed tenure. Direct-recruitment posts can be regular - the notification states the nature of each post, so check before applying.

6. Are there bank jobs without an exam?

A few. Some banks fill specialist and local officer posts through shortlisting plus interview. Bank apprenticeship drives vary - some are merit-based while others include an online test - so read each notification's selection clause.

7. Are there railway jobs without an exam?

Yes: Act Apprentice intakes (merit list), sports quota, cultural quota and Scouts & Guides quota. Apprentice intakes are large; the quota routes are small zonal recruitments with their own assessment process.

8. Is India Post GDS really without an exam?

Yes - selection is an online merit list generated from Class 10 marks, with no exam and no interview. Because of that, GDS is heavily targeted by paid-selection scams; apply only through the official GDS portal.

9. How do I identify fake "no exam" job offers?

No genuine government post is sold, fees are paid only on official portals, and no recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram messages. Verify every offer against the official notification on a government or PSU domain - if it isn't there, it's fraud.

10. How often is this list updated?

Daily. New notifications are added as they release, and every listing is removed automatically after its last date, so the list only ever shows posts you can still apply for.

Govt Jobs for Law Graduates - Eligibility (LLB, LLM, BL)

Eligibility varies by post, but the core requirement for almost every government law job is a recognised law degree. Senior and specialised roles add experience, an LLM, or Bar enrolment on top.

Educational Qualification

  • Bachelor of Law (BL) / LLB (Legum Baccalaureus): the baseline qualification for most legal and law officer posts.
  • LLM (Master of Laws): required for senior legal officer, faculty, and some advisory positions.
  • Integrated 5-year degrees - BA LLB, BBA LLB, BCom LLB - are accepted wherever an LLB is required.

The degree must be from a university recognised by the Bar Council of India.

Bar Council Enrolment & AIBE

For litigation, prosecutor, and standing-counsel roles you generally need to be enrolled as an advocate with a State Bar Council, and many positions ask for the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) Certificate of Practice issued by the Bar Council of India. Purely advisory or research posts (Law Clerk, Research Fellow, Legal Consultant) often do not require enrolment.

Age Limit & Relaxations

The upper age limit is typically 30 to 40 years for the general category, depending on the post and recruiter. Statutory relaxations apply: usually 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC/ST, and additional relaxation for PwD and ex-servicemen candidates. Always confirm the exact limit and cut-off date in the official notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

Salary & Pay Scale for Government Law Jobs

Pay depends on the organisation and grade. Officer-level legal posts under the 7th Pay Commission generally fall in Pay Levels 10 to 12, with a monthly salary roughly between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500, plus Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, and other benefits. PSU legal officers are paid on IDA scales, which can be higher at entry grade.

Types of Law Officer / Legal Posts in Government Sector

  • Judicial Services - Civil Judge (Junior Division), Additional District Judge, High Court Judge, recruited via State Judicial Service Exams (PCS-J)
  • Law Officer / Legal Officer - Roles in public sector banks (IBPS SO Law), insurance companies (LIC AAO Legal), regulatory bodies (SEBI Grade A Legal), and PSUs (Coal India, NTPC, GAIL Legal)
  • Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor - Administrative legal support roles in ministries, universities, and district courts
  • Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO) - Prosecution roles recruited through State PSCs, requiring LLB and often a minimum years of practice

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, ADJ, High Court Judge)

Judicial Services is the most prestigious and highest-paying career path for LLB graduates. Recruitment happens through State Public Service Commissions (e.g., RPSC, UPPSC, MPPSC) via a three-stage exam: Preliminary, Mains, and Interview. Civil Judge posts typically require 0-3 years of practice depending on the state, while some states allow fresh LLB graduates to apply directly.

Law Officer / Legal Officer (Banks, PSU, Insurance)

Public sector banks and insurance companies recruit Law Officers through specialist officer (SO) exams. These posts require only an LLB degree (AIBE not mandatory) and offer competitive pay scales under the 7th Pay Commission equivalent structure, along with allowances.

Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor Posts

These are typically Group B/C administrative-legal posts in ministries, universities, and PSU legal departments, requiring an LLB degree and sometimes relevant drafting/litigation experience.

Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO)

APO recruitment is conducted by State PSCs (e.g., RPSC Assistant Prosecution Officer) and requires an LLB degree, enrollment as an advocate, and in most states, a minimum period of practice (often 3 years).

Selection Process for Law Govt Jobs

The selection process differs by post but commonly includes:

  1. Written examination - testing legal knowledge, aptitude, and general awareness (for judicial services and most exam-based posts).
  2. Interview / viva-voce - assessing legal reasoning and suitability.
  3. Document verification - degree, Bar enrolment, AIBE, age, and category certificates.

Advisory and consultant posts are often filled by shortlisting and interview alone, without a written exam.

How to Apply for Law Govt Jobs

  2. Open the official notification and read the eligibility, fee, and important dates.
  3. Register on the recruiter's official portal.
  4. Fill in the application with your LLB/LLM, Bar enrolment, and personal details.
  5. Upload the required documents and photograph.
  6. Pay the application fee (if any) and submit before the last date.
  7. Save or print the confirmation for future reference.

Each row in the table links directly to the official notification, so you can apply from the source.

Law Govt Jobs FAQ's

What are the latest law govt jobs in 2026?

Current law government jobs in 2026 include Law Officer, Legal Officer, Assistant Prosecution Officer, Judicial Service, and Legal Adviser posts across High Courts, PSUs, public sector banks, and central/state departments. The table above is updated daily with vacancy count, last date, and the official notification link.

Which departments hire LLB and law graduates?

High Courts and District Courts, the Ministry of Law and Justice, UPSC, State Public Service Commissions, public sector banks, PSUs, insurance companies, and regulatory bodies regularly recruit law graduates for legal and judicial roles.

What is the eligibility for government law jobs?

Most posts require a Bachelor of Law (LLB/BL) from a recognised university; senior roles may require LLM and experience. Litigation and prosecutor posts usually require enrolment with a State Bar Council and, often, the AIBE certificate.

What is the salary of a Law Officer in the government sector?

A government Law Officer or Legal Officer typically earns between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500 per month under the 7th Pay Commission, depending on the organisation, plus DA, HRA, and allowances. PSU legal officers draw IDA-scale pay.

Can a fresher LLB graduate get a government job?

Yes. Freshers can apply for Civil Judge (Junior Division) judicial-service exams, Law Clerk and Research Fellow posts in High Courts, and trainee legal roles. Some PSU and bank Law Officer posts require a few years of post-enrolment experience.

How can I apply for law officer vacancies in central government?

Open the post in the table above, read the official notification, register on the recruiter's portal, fill in the application with your LLB and enrolment details, pay the fee, and submit before the last date.

What is the difference between Judicial Services and Law Officer posts

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, via state judiciary exams) places you on the bench as a judge. Law Officer/Legal Officer posts are departmental legal-counsel roles in PSUs, banks, and ministries - advisory and litigation support, recruited by interview or written test.

Is there an age limit for govt law jobs?

Most posts set the upper age at 30 to 40 years for the general category, with statutory relaxations for OBC, SC/ST, and PwD candidates. Check each notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

How to Check Your OnlyJobs 2026 Online (Step-by-Step)

Checking a OnlyJobs result takes only a few minutes once you know the steps:

  • Find your exam in the Latest Results section below, or use the search bar to type the exam name (e.g., "SSC CGL" or "RRB NTPC").
  • Read the result summary to confirm the post, organisation, and result date.
  • Open the official portal link provided in the article (e.g., ssc.nic.in, upsc.gov.in).
  • Enter your Roll Number or Registration ID along with your date of birth, as required by that exam body.
  • Download or screenshot your result/scorecard for future reference - most government portals remove results after a few weeks.
  • Check the next stage (cut-off, document verification, interview call letter) - OnlyJobs lists this under the same exam tag so you can track the full recruitment cycle.

Note: If the official server is busy on result day, wait a few minutes and try again rather than refreshing repeatedly; heavy traffic is normal in the first hour after a major result is declared.

SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026 - Download Link, Interview Dates & Full Details

The State Bank of India (SBI) has officially released the SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026 on 4 July 2026, and candidates who cleared the online examination for the Circle Based Officer (CBO) post can now download it from the official portal. As per the notice, the SBI CBO interview will be held from 13 July 2026 to 19 July 2026. If you're one of the shortlisted candidates, this is your final step before securing a role as a Circle Based Officer at SBI so let's walk through everything you need to know: where to download the call letter, what documents to carry, and how the final selection is calculated.

Add FJA on  As Preferred Source

SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026 - Quick Overview

This section summarizes the most important facts about the SBI CBO 2026 interview round in one place, so you can quickly confirm the key dates and numbers without scrolling through the entire article.

Particulars Details
Recruiting Body State Bank of India (SBI)
Post Name Circle Based Officer (CBO)
Advertisement No. CRPD/CBO/2025-26/18
Total Vacancies 2,050
Interview Call Letter Release Date 4 July 2026
Interview Dates 13 July 2026 to 19 July 2026
Selection Stages Online Exam → Screening → Interview → Local Language Proficiency Test
Marks Allotted for Interview 50 Marks
Final Merit Weightage Online Test: 75% + Interview: 25%
Starting Basic Pay ₹48,480 + 2 Advance Increments

What Is the SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026?

Before downloading your admit card, it helps to understand exactly what this document is and why it matters for the recruitment process. The SBI CBO Interview Call Letter is the official admission ticket that confirms a candidate has cleared the earlier stages and is now eligible to appear for the personal interview round.

The interview call letter is a mandatory document for the SBI CBO Recruitment 2026 drive, which is being conducted to fill 2,050 vacancies for the Circle Based Officer post across various states and language zones. Without this call letter, candidates will not be permitted entry into the interview venue, so downloading and verifying it well in advance is essential.

SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026: Download Link

This section explains exactly where and how you can access your call letter online, along with what to do immediately after downloading it.

Candidates can download the SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026 through the official recruitment portal. Once downloaded, cross-check every detail printed on it including your interview date, reporting time, and venue address and keep both a printed copy and a digital backup ready ahead of interview day.

Click Here to Download SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026

Login Credentials Required to Download the Call Letter

To successfully access your call letter, you'll need specific login credentials that were created during your application process. This section lists exactly what you need to have on hand.

You will need the following details to log in to the portal:

  • Registration Number or Roll Number (generated at the time of application/exam)
  • Password or Date of Birth (as set/used during registration)

Since these credentials were generated earlier in the recruitment cycle, candidates who have misplaced them should retrieve their registration details before the download window gets busy closer to the interview dates.

How to Download SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026: Step-by-Step

If you're downloading your call letter for the first time, this simple step-by-step guide will help you complete the process without errors.

  1. Visit the official SBI website or the direct download link provided above.
  2. Navigate to the "Careers" section (if accessing via sbi.co.in).
  3. Click on the SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026 link.
  4. Enter your Registration Number/Roll Number and Password/Date of Birth.
  5. Click submit to view your call letter.
  6. Download the PDF and take a clear printout for the interview day.

Details Mentioned on the SBI CBO Interview Call Letter

Your call letter contains critical information you must verify immediately after downloading. This section breaks down exactly what's printed on the document.

The SBI CBO Interview Call Letter 2026 includes:

  • Candidate's name and roll number
  • Interview date and reporting time
  • Interview venue name and complete address
  • Important day-of instructions and guidelines

If any detail such as your name, photograph, or center address appears incorrect, contact the SBI recruitment cell or IBPS helpline immediately for correction.

Also Read: UP Home Guard DV/PST Admit Card 2026

Documents to Carry for the SBI CBO Interview 2026

Carrying the correct set of documents is non-negotiable for interview-day entry. This section lists everything you must bring along.

  • A printed copy of the interview call letter
  • A valid original photo ID proof (Aadhaar, PAN, Passport, Voter ID, etc.)
  • Original and photocopies of educational certificates and mark sheets
  • Recent passport-size photographs (the same one used during application, if specified)

Candidates should keep all documents organized in a single folder to avoid last-minute confusion at the venue.

SBI CBO 2026 Selection Process Explained

Understanding how your final selection is calculated helps you prepare strategically for the interview. This section explains the complete selection methodology for SBI CBO 2026.

The SBI Circle Based Officer recruitment follows a multi-stage selection process:

  1. Online Examination - The first screening stage testing candidates' aptitude and knowledge.
  2. Screening/Shortlisting - Candidates are shortlisted based on online exam performance for the interview stage.
  3. Interview - Worth 50 marks, assessing banking awareness, professional knowledge, and communication skills.
  4. Local Language Proficiency Test - Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in the regional/local language relevant to their applied state or circle.

How Is the Final Merit List Prepared?

The final selection isn't based on the interview alone it combines scores from multiple stages using a fixed weightage formula.

The final merit list for SBI CBO 2026 is prepared using combined weightage:

  • Online Examination: 75% weightage
  • Interview: 25% weightage

This means strong performance in the online exam significantly boosts your overall chances, but a good interview score remains essential for the final cutoff.

SBI CBO Salary and Pay Scale 2026

Many candidates preparing for the interview also want clarity on the compensation structure for this role.

Selected Circle Based Officers will receive a starting basic pay of ₹48,480, along with 2 advance increments, as per the official SBI CBO notification. For a full salary breakup including allowances and in-hand pay, refer to the SBI CBO Salary details.

SBI CBO Recruitment 2026: Background Details

A quick refresher on the recruitment cycle helps put the interview call letter in context for candidates tracking the full timeline.

Event Date
Online Application Start 29 January 2026
Online Application Last Date 25 February 2026 (Extended)
Online Exam Admit Card 6 March 2026
Online Examination Date 14 March 2026
Result Declared 30 June 2026
Interview Call Letter Released 4 July 2026
Interview Dates 13-19 July 2026

The recruitment drive (Advt. No. CRPD/CBO/2025-26/18) targets 2,050 Circle Based Officer vacancies distributed across multiple states, with eligibility requiring a bachelor's degree in any stream along with knowledge of the local language of the respective state/circle applied for. The minimum age is 21 years and the maximum age is 30 years, as reckoned on 31 December 2025.

What to Do After the SBI CBO Interview?

Once your interview is complete, there are a few more stages before you receive your final appointment. Candidates should track official SBI communication for updates on Document Verification and Medical Examination, which typically follow the interview stage before the final selection and joining process.

Indian Army Agniveer Result 2026 is expected to be released in the first week of July 2026 on the official Join Indian Army website, joinindianarmy.nic.in. The Indian Army conducted the Agniveer Common Entrance Examination (CEE) 2026 from 1 June to 16 June 2026 for posts including Agniveer General Duty, Technical, Clerk, Tradesman, and Women Military Police. As of now, the result has not been officially declared. Once released, candidates will be able to check their qualifying status using their roll number or name in the result PDF. This page will be updated immediately with the direct download link and merit list details as soon as the Indian Army makes an official announcement.

Indian Army Agniveer Result 2026 Overview

Candidates who appeared for the Agniveer CEE 2026 can refer to the table below for a quick summary of the key details related to the Indian Army Agniveer Result 2026.

Conducting Body Indian Army

Final Selection Agniveer Final Merit List 2026

Event Date

Indian Army Agniveer Result 2026 Expected first week of July 2026
Phase 2 Process (PFT, PMT, Medical) To be announced after result declaration

The Indian Army Agniveer Result 2026 download link will be activated on the official Join Indian Army website after the result is officially declared. Candidates who appeared for the CEE 2026 will be able to download the result PDF directly from the official portal. The link on this page will be updated immediately once it goes live.

Indian Army Agniveer Result 2026 Direct Link: Active Soon

Indian Army Agniveer Zone Wise / ARO Wise Result 2026

The Indian Army releases regional merit lists separately for each Army Recruitment Office (ARO) across different states. Candidates should check the result specific to the ARO where they appeared for the recruitment rally or CEE. Zone-wise results for AROs in states such as Bihar, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Odisha, West Bengal, Haryana, Jammu and Kashmir, and Punjab are expected to be released along with or shortly after the main result declaration. All zone-wise links are currently marked as To Be Announced (TBA) and will be updated once the Indian Army activates them.

Eligibility Criteria

Educational Qualification

Educational qualification requirements vary by Agniveer category (General Duty, Technical, Clerk, Tradesman) and were specified in the original Agniveer CEE 2026 recruitment notification. Candidates should refer to their respective category's official notification for exact qualification details, as this information was not part of the result announcement.

Age Limit

Age limit criteria for Agniveer recruitment 2026 were defined in the official recruitment notification issued prior to the CEE. Candidates are advised to check the original notification on joinindianarmy.nic.in for category-wise age limit details.

Selection Process

The Indian Army Agniveer selection process consists of the following stages:

  1. Agniveer Common Entrance Examination (CEE) – Online CBT
  2. Physical Fitness Test (PFT)
  3. Physical Measurement Test (PMT)
  4. Medical Examination
  5. Document Verification
  6. Final Merit List

Candidates who qualify the written CEE will be shortlisted for the Phase 2 process, which includes the PFT, PMT, and Medical Examination. Final selection depends on performance across all stages combined into the Agniveer Final Merit List 2026.

How to Check Indian Army Agniveer Result 2026

Follow the steps below to check and download the Indian Army Agniveer Result 2026 once it is released:

  1. Visit the official Join Indian Army website, joinindianarmy.nic.in.
  2. On the homepage, scroll down and click on the Agniveer section.
  3. Find and click on the "Indian Army Agniveer Result 2026" link.
  4. The result PDF will open on the screen.
  5. Use the search (Ctrl+F) option to find your roll number or name in the PDF.
  6. Download the result PDF and keep a printout or screenshot for future reference.

Indian Army Agniveer Phase 2 Recruitment Process 2026

Candidates shortlisted in the Agniveer Result 2026 will be called for the Phase 2 recruitment process, which evaluates physical fitness, physical standards, and medical fitness.

Physical Fitness Test (PFT)

The Physical Fitness Test evaluates a candidate's endurance and strength through a timed run, pull-ups, a 9-feet ditch jump, and zig-zag balance. Candidates are grouped based on their running time, and marks are awarded accordingly for the run and pull-up events, while the ditch and balance events are qualifying in nature.

Group 1.6 Km Run Time Marks for Run Pull-Ups Marks for Pull-Ups 9 Feet Ditch Zig-Zag Balance
Group I Up to 5 min 30 sec 60 10 40 Qualifying Qualifying
Group II 5 min 31 sec to 5 min 45 sec 48 9 33 Qualifying Qualifying
- - - 8 27 Qualifying Qualifying
- - - 7 21 Qualifying Qualifying
- - - 6 16 Qualifying Qualifying

Physical Measurement Test (PMT)

The PMT checks whether candidates meet the physical standards prescribed by the Indian Army for height, chest, and weight based on category and region.

Parameter Requirement
Height As per Army standards for the respective category
Chest Required chest expansion as prescribed
Weight Proportionate to height and age as per Army standards

Medical Examination

The Medical Examination ensures that candidates are medically fit for service in the Indian Army. Only medically fit candidates are considered for the final merit list.

Medical Standard Requirement
Eyesight As per Army medical standards
Hearing Normal hearing ability
Chest X-ray Must be clear and satisfactory
Blood and Urine Tests Must meet prescribed medical standards
Tattoos No permanent tattoos except in permitted areas
Overall Fitness Must be medically fit as per Indian Army norms

Required Documents

Candidates shortlisted in the Agniveer Result 2026 should keep the following documents ready for the Phase 2 process and document verification:

  • Admit Card of Agniveer CEE 2026
  • Result printout or screenshot
  • Original and photocopies of educational certificates
  • Valid government-issued photo ID proof
  • Domicile or residence certificate, if applicable
  • Recent passport-size photographs
  • Character certificate, if required

  • The Indian Army Agniveer Result 2026 has not yet been officially released as of the date of this article.
  • Only check the result on the official website, joinindianarmy.nic.in, to avoid misinformation.
  • Keep your roll number and registered details handy for a quick search once the result is out.
  • Download and save the result PDF immediately after release, as links may be updated periodically.
  • Shortlisted candidates should start preparing for the Physical Fitness Test in advance.
  • Bookmark this page for real-time updates on the result and merit list.
